text:
Maya - Product: FYI — Large enterprise (Finovo) pushed for a contractual SLO: 99.99% uptime + p95 latency <= 150ms for hosted API, plus 24/7 premium support. Asking product for triage and routing.
Alex - Sales: They want it in contract this quarter, legal is pushing for committable numbers. They also said data must stay in EU region.
Hao - SRE: 99.99% is doable but depends on deployment mode. For hosted multitenant we'd need capacity reservations or Dedicated pools in region + cross-region failover. Need to quantify cost delta.
Lina - Eng: p95 150ms is tight for large seq gen across models. We should ask which endpoints (textgen vs embeddings) and seq length distribution. For chat short prompts maybe fine; long-context requests will blow up.
Tara - Support: 24/7 premium -> we need an on-call rotation and escalation path. Who owns first-response SLA? Also need runbooks and P1 playbook before we sign.
Sam - Legal: Contracts want clear definitions and remedies. Please provide precise SLO language + measurement window + exclusion list (maintenance, DDoS, customer-caused).
Maya - Product: Agreed. Proposal: 1) Offer two productized options: Hosted Premium SLA (in-region Dedicated capacity + 24/7 support) OR Private (VPC) with customer-managed infra. 2) Draft SLO spec for legal. 3) Cost delta + impact on roadmap.
Alex - Sales: Customer prefers hosted but with data residency. If Hosted Premium is an option, need price & committed throughput. They estimate 500 reqs/s peak EU.
Hao - SRE: Important to capture traffic profile. Suggest load test scenario: 500 rps sustained, 5k concurrent KV sessions. Also need autoscale warmup and burst policy.
Lina - Eng: For me to sign off on p95 150ms we need: - quantized model variant with latency profile validated - reserved GPU pool <-> no noisy neighbor - KV cache + prefix caching for common prompts. I'll draft an acceptance checklist.
Maya - Product: Draft SLO spec (first pass) below. Can people comment?
Maya - Product: ```
SLO: Hosted Premium EU
- Availability: 99.99% monthly (measured at edge load-balancer)
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for text-generation endpoint (seq <= 512 tokens)
- Support: 24/7 premium P1 response <= 30m, mitigation update <= 4h
Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (48h notice), customer-network issues, force majeure
Measurement: monthly window, standard telemetry from CDN + runtime traces
Rollout criteria: capacity tests pass at 1.5x expected peak, runbooks validated, canary 72h no regression
```
Sam - Legal: This is a good start. Add remedy tiers (credits), and require targeted SLA for data residency audits + access to audit logs. Also define the measurement points and ownership of metrics.
Tara - Support: Add: escalation contact list + playbook link. Also include a runbook for token-quota degradation and a fallback plan (model variant degrade) to keep availability.
Hao - SRE: Note: we should allow automated fallback to lower-latency model variant (quantized). Fallback behavior must be explicit in contract (so customers understand quality tradeoff).
Alex - Sales: Customer will likely accept fallback as long as we notify them and have a rollback window. Also they asked about penalty caps.
Maya - Product: Action items: @Lina to draft acceptance checklist (due in 48h). @Hao to estimate infra + cost delta for 500rps peak + 1.5x buffer (due 72h). @Sam to prepare contract language template (72h). @Tara to prepare support runbook stub (48h). I'll assemble a one-pager for Sales to share.
Lina - Eng: Got it — will include perf numbers by model variant and required GPU types.
Hao - SRE: I'll include autoscale warmup, regional capacity reservation options, and recovery RTO/RPO assumptions.
Sam - Legal: I'll draft exclusion list + credit table. Quick Q: do we want to tie credits to monthly uptime only or to latency as well?
Maya - Product: Prefer to tie credits primarily to availability; latency breaches get operational remediation + escalation first, credits as last resort. But willing to discuss for P0 customers.
Alex - Sales: Customer wants both, but availability is the bigger concern. We'll escalate to execs if needed.
Oncall Bot: Incident policy link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/sla-playbook (automated)
Tara - Support: Also flagging onboarding checklist: access to logs, support contacts, runbook readout session, and SOAR integration if requested.
Maya - Product: I'll open a tracker ticket with owners and timeline. Any objections to this path?
Alex - Sales: No objections. Thanks team. I'll prep customer-facing options.
Lina - Eng: No objections. Will add notes about model quality tradeoffs to product one-pager.
Hao - SRE: No objections. Will send capacity estimate + TL;DR for pricing.
Sam - Legal: No objections. Will sync with sales on penalty caps.
Maya - Product: Great — meeting to review drafts Friday 10am UTC. Closing thread for now. :thumbsup:
